result.capability: Native bridge end: extension background calls browser.runtime.sendNativeMessage; the native app extension's SafariWebExtensionHandler (a separate process from the containing app) handles beginRequest/completeRequest (request/response only); results reach the containing app via an App Group container or the backend
result.environment: Documentation review only (accessed 2026-09-28 UTC); reference iPadOS 27.0 (24A437), Safari 27.0, Xcode 27 (27A266a). No build, install, provider call or device run.
result.limitation: Content scripts cannot call it; the iOS containing app cannot push to extension JavaScript. Handler payload/memory/time limits are undocumented (Apple engineer forum reply: 80 MB in 15.1). Apple documents only the message (SFExtensionMessageKey) and, on 17+, a Safari profile UUID (SFExtensionProfileKey) in the handler's userInfo; no sender tab/URL/origin is documented (inferred from silence; DT-G1-09 logs observed keys). Page origin must therefore come from the extension background (runtime.MessageSender), which v0.1.0 BridgeRequest cannot carry (lead request).
result.fallback: Extension calls the backend over HTTPS directly with pairing auth (no native bridge). Since Safari 18.4 this needs the user to grant the backend origin (browser.permissions.request) or backend CORS accepting the extension origin (D1-M01). The app reads results from the backend.
